summary: New Zealand lets visa-waiver nationals (including the US, UK, EU countries, Canada and Japan) visit for up to 3 months — 6 for British citizens — but they must first obtain an NZeTA, and most international visitors also pay the NZD 100 International Visitor Levy. Australians enter freely, everyone else needs a Visitor Visa, and everyone travelling into New Zealand must complete a New Zealand Traveller Declaration; New Zealand Customs suggests doing the digital declaration before the flight, and for air travellers it needs to be submitted by the time they reach passport control.

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read makes travel insurance an entry requirement. Immigration New Zealand says visitors will need to pay for any health care or medical assistance they need in New Zealand, and recommends full medical insurance for the stay.

onwardTicket.text: Immigration New Zealand says NZeTA travellers must be able to show at check-in for a flight to New Zealand that they intend to leave at the end of their stay: a paid ticket out of New Zealand to a country they have the right to enter, or a cruise itinerary or craft owner's letter if leaving by sea. To apply for a Visitor Visa, it says, you must show you can leave New Zealand at the end of your stay.

declarations.name: New Zealand Traveller Declaration (NZTD)
declarations.submitWindow: By air: from 24 hours before you start your trip until you reach passport control in New Zealand. By sea: from 24 hours before departing the vessel’s last foreign port until it berths at its first New Zealand port.
declarations.text: Everyone travelling into New Zealand, including New Zealand passport holders, must complete the free New Zealand Traveller Declaration (website or app), which collects travel, customs, immigration and biosecurity information. Air travellers can submit it from 24 hours before they start their trip, and it needs to be submitted by the time they reach passport control in New Zealand; New Zealand Customs suggests doing it before the flight to make arrival easier. It is linked to your passport and checked at the eGate or by a border officer; you do not need to print anything.

notes: The UK says it is illegal to import most food products into New Zealand and that you must declare anything that may be prohibited; breaking the rules can mean a fine of up to NZ$100,000 or a prison sentence.

Wood and leather products, golf clubs, tents and fishing equipment can carry pests or diseases, the UK says: if in doubt, declare them to a Biosecurity New Zealand official or put them in the marked bins at the airport.

safety.text: The UK FCDO says crime levels are generally low, but street crime happens in major towns and cities and thieves may target unattended vehicles, especially hire cars and camper vans in tourist areas. It says New Zealand is in a major earthquake zone, that tsunamis can happen along the coastlines, and that weather can quickly become dangerous in some coastal and exposed areas.

tips.text: New Zealand's Ministry for Primary Industries says some foods, drinks, sports and outdoor equipment can carry harmful pests and diseases, and that if you're unsure you should declare your items when you arrive or put them in the bin, otherwise you can get a fine. The UK says it is illegal to import most food products, that tents, fishing equipment and golf clubs can carry pests, and that breaking the rules can mean a fine of up to NZ$100,000 or a prison sentence.

Complete the free New Zealand Traveller Declaration online or in the NZTD app before your flight: New Zealand Customs suggests it to make arrival easier, says everyone travelling into New Zealand must complete one, and says it needs to be submitted by the time you reach passport control.

Canada says traffic drives on the left. The UK notes that highways can be narrow, winding and hilly, and Canada warns that rural railway crossings may have no barriers and that dairy herds often cross main roads at milking time.

Budget for the NZD 100 International Visitor Levy on top of the NZeTA fee (from NZD 17): the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment says most international visitors pay it when applying for a visa or NZeTA, and that it funds conservation, infrastructure used for tourism and other tourism initiatives.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for New Zealand?
faq.answer: No visa, but they must request an NZeTA before boarding (from NZD 17), and most international visitors also pay the NZD 100 International Visitor Levy. Once granted, it is valid for 2 years and allows visits of up to 3 months.

faq.question: How much does the NZeTA really cost?
faq.answer: Immigration New Zealand gives the NZeTA cost as from NZD 17 and says to use the official NZeTA website or app. The Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment says most international visitors also pay the NZD 100 International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy (IVL), when applying for a visa or NZeTA.

faq.question: Do Australians need an NZeTA or visa for New Zealand?
faq.answer: No. Immigration New Zealand says Australian citizens need neither a visa nor an NZeTA. It lists Australian permanent residents among the travellers who can visit New Zealand on an NZeTA.

faq.question: What is the New Zealand Traveller Declaration?
faq.answer: The NZTD is a free declaration that everyone travelling into New Zealand must complete, online at travellerdeclaration.govt.nz or in the NZTD app. It collects travel, customs, immigration and biosecurity information and replaces the old Passenger Arrival Card. New Zealand Customs suggests doing the digital declaration before your flight instead of filling in a paper declaration onboard; for air travellers it needs to be submitted by the time you reach passport control.

faq.question: How long can I stay in New Zealand as a visitor?
faq.answer: Immigration New Zealand says NZeTA visitors from visa waiver countries can stay up to 3 months per visit (6 months on a UK passport), and no more than 6 months within any 12-month period. For longer stays, it says a Visitor Visa lets you stay for up to 6 or 9 months, with a maximum of 9 months in an 18-month period.
